newsitem.title: USA: CME March, May lumber futures end with limit gains.
newsitem.headline: CME March, May lumber futures end with limit gains.

text.p: CME March and May lumber futures closed with limit gains of $10.00 per thousand board feet and July closed up $9.90 amid talk of increased cash sales, CME traders said.

However, one analyst said technical factors rather than fundamental ones caused the limit gains. Early selling failed to test support at $390 in March, prompting short covering, said Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures Trading.
"I do not see any improvement in cash (markets)," he said. "It (cash market) is still quite quiet."
Cunningham said he expects robust demand once the weather moderates because dealers have very low inventories.
When the spring building develops these dealers will be rushing to buy wood.
"All the business will try to be run through the keyhole at once," he said.
However, for the moment, dealers are content to operate with the low lumber supplies, he said.
CME traders estimated about 20 unfilled contracts remained in the March and none remained in May.
CME lumber closed up $10.00 to $1.90 per tbf with March at $403.50 and May at $387.50.
